Set automatic selectivity prior parameters in data object

Source: R/BLICC_blip.R
blip_sel_auto.Rd

The priors for each function are defined loosely based on the available data ("empirical Bayes"). It is recommended that priors are weakly informative, so they are set primarily to aid fitting and discourage values outside a reasonable range.

Usage

blip_sel_auto(blicc_ld, sel_indx = NULL)

Arguments

blicc_ld

A standard data list suitable for the model (see function blicc_dat)

sel_indx

An integer vector index of the selectivity functions to be changed. If not provided, all functions will be replaced.

Value

The data object blicc_ld but with the new selectivity priors

Details

The prior hyper-parameters are "estimated" if there is a single selectivity for a gear. The estimates are based on the 50% (median), 10% and 90% quartiles of the cumulative frequency. This ensures that the selectivity function is centred on the frequency data and provides a robust estimate of reasonable priors. Alternatively, setting parameters manually can be done using the blip_sel function.

If a selectivity is made up of a mixture of functions, prior parameters are not estimated and blip_sel must be used to set the parameters manually. This is necessary because the user must propose the hypothesis for the mixtures and it cannot easily be determined from the data what a suitable hypothesis might be.

Examples

new_ld <- blip_sel_auto(gillnet_ld)
